title: 马诗·其五
author: 李贺
intro: Desert sand white as snow, a hook of moon over the mountains: a fine horse dreams of a golden bridle and a gallop across the clear autumn plain — and so does the poet.
analysis: 李贺写过二十三首《马诗》，这是第五首，统编教材选入。前两句写边塞夜景：大沙漠里的沙子在月光下白得像雪，燕山上的月亮弯弯的像一把钩子。“钩”是古代一种弯刀，所以这句也暗含打仗的味道。后两句是马的心愿：什么时候能给我戴上金子装饰的笼头，让我在清爽的秋天原野上奔驰？表面写马，其实写人：好马盼望遇到懂它的主人，诗人盼望得到重用、为国家建功立业。这种借物写自己的手法叫“托物言志”。“快走踏清秋”一句很有速度感，读起来像听见了马蹄声。
analysisEn: Li He wrote a set of 23 horse poems; this is No. 5, the one taught in Chinese schools. The first two lines show a frontier night: under the moon the desert sand is white as snow, and over the Yan Mountains hangs a moon curved like a hook. A 钩 was also a curved sabre, so the line carries a hint of battle. The last two lines are the horse’s wish: when will someone put a gold-trimmed bridle on me, so I can gallop across the clear autumn plain? It is about a horse, but really about a man. A fine horse longs for a master who knows its worth; the poet longs for a ruler who will put his talents to use. Speaking about yourself through an object like this is called 托物言志. Listen to the last line — 快走踏清秋 — and you can almost hear hooves striking the ground.
background: Li He (790–816) was a brilliant, sickly poet of royal descent who was barred from the imperial exams on a technicality and died at 26. His horse poems are often read as his frustration at having talent no one would use.
pronunciation: 燕山 yān（地名，不读 yàn）。何当 hé dāng。络脑 luò。
version: 采用通行版本（统编教材）。原组诗共二十三首，每首独立成篇，网站收第五首。

lines.lit: In the great desert, the sand is like snow;
lines.en: The desert sand lies white as snow;

lines.lit: over the Yan Mountains, the moon is like a hook.
lines.en: over the Yan Mountains, a hook of moon.

lines.lit: When shall I wear a golden bridle,
lines.en: When will they put a gold bridle on me

lines.lit: and run fast, treading the clear autumn?
lines.en: and let me race across the clear autumn plain?

words.note: 现代汉语书面语还用，“大漠孤烟”。
读 yān；古代是边塞地区。
古代说法，现代汉语说“什么时候”。
古代说法，现代汉语说“笼头”。
古义是“跑”，和今天的“走（walk）”不同。

imagery.name: 马
imagery.zh: 好马盼望被人赏识、驰骋疆场，比喻诗人渴望施展才能。
imagery.en: The fine horse longs to be recognised and to race into battle — just as the poet longs to use his talents.

imagery.name: 月
imagery.zh: 弯月像弯刀，冷冷地挂在边塞上空，带出战场的气氛。
imagery.en: The crescent moon, like a curved blade over the frontier, sets a battlefield mood.
